Side Hustle

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The typical 9-5 job as we know it is slowing dying out, more and more professionals are seeking fulfilment in side hustles.

Unique Selling Point:
Whether it's a passion project or the monthly salary is no longer enough to make ends meet, it's becoming common for professionals to pursue alternate interests. Side hustles refers to people who are employed but create a king of enterprise outside of their working hours. SOuth Africa, although still very traditional in it approaches the professional working life, is seeing a growing trend of people getting into side hustles.

Summary:
The piece will profile three side hustlers.
Thresh out a research out report by Jon Foster-Pedley from Henley Business School about the trends of side hustling in South Africa and how the corporate world in responding to it as well as economic benefits.
An interview with a 'work analyst' give details about the kind of side hustles that are popular or that can be pursued without disrupting people's professional careers.


Further information:
We'll include an aspect of MacFarlene's life as somebody who continues to work in radio broadcasting as a side hustle, a platform he both loves and adds extra cash to his life.
Treatment: business magazine feel, short and dynamic links as well as interactive interviews. Do some of the interviews whilst the side hustlers are doing their hustling activities and get Mac to participate.

Script:


VO
Up sound
Visuals
The traditional professional life of showing up at your job and spending the compulsory 8 hours toiling away is slowly becoming outdated. Employees want more, more money, flexibility and a chance to explore their passions. This is changing the way we work

Bryan Davey has been an engine and generator specialist for 16 years, a hands on and gruelling job. His expertise sees him working on a variety of machines,from industrial generators, big trucks, and even small automotive engines.




To help him destress Bryan started baking, a hobby he wasn’t initially good at. He would ask his family and friends for feedback on his cupcakes and specialty desserts and after several attempts and a growing confidence, Bryan officially started his small bakery, the grizzly baker.



Balancing a demanding career with a busy side hustle keeps Dr Katlego Lekalakala going.
She’s one of the intern doctors at Charlotte Maxeke hospital. She is currently doing her surgery rotation, one of the most challenging specialties.
When Dr Lekalakal is not spending long hours on her feet during rounds at one of the biggest hospitals in the country, she pursues her side hustle as a makeup artist


Self-taught, with a large following on social media, Dr Lekalakala has become one of Johannesburg’s sought after make up artists. Her clientele ranges from celebrities, brides, well known brands for adverts and women who want to look beautiful for special occasions.



Last year Henley Business School conducted research in South Africa and the United Kingdom analysing this new phenomenon. Jon Foster-Pedley, was the at the forefront of this study




Research indicates that side hustling allows people to learn new skills that they otherwise would not learn from their main job. Such as becoming proficient in running a business. According to the study by the Henley Business School, side-hustlers become more focused and enthusiastic about their main jobs.
And this Foster-Pedley says is good for both the employer and employee



From freelance writing, teaching English online or creating apps all of which can bring in a decent extra income.

Scelo Makhathini is the CEO of LinkedPro an online platform that links professionals seeking freelance jobs to potential employers
Makhathini says the internet will disrupt how we work in the future







Mac - A Day in the life of Bryan, what does that entail
Bryan - Wake up at four in the morning, go through straight to work by 6, get my parts...





Mac - You’re a mechanic and now you’re a baker but this baking turned into a business right
Byran - So the transition sort of happened after I started getting better at it
Mac - How did you know you were getting better because obviously if you’re making your fiance and your parents taste they don’t wanna let you down
Bryan - (pick him up at) What I started doing was I just gave it to random people at work, random people that I knew (Mac interjects) but then I they said okay good this is actually quite tasty. So they said why don’t you try make it into a business. So I started getting more in dept, so, so research as in youtube videos, how to do certain things, finding recipes
I am dabbling a lil bit now with wedding cakes, I’ve done three wedding cakes so far
Mac: Aaah and those people are still marries
Bryan: Yes
Mac: Okay cool, that means the cake was good.
Bryan: Actually one o my wedding cakes did feature in a wedding magazine



Katlego: We’re not panel beating, we’re just fixing a screw




Mac Question – how do you choose between the two are you first a doctor or a make up artist

Katelgo – I guess I am first a doctor cause that’s my title, I would love to do them both but being a doctor takes up a lot of my time
Mac: The kind of event, place or the kind of environment the person will be in, does that also influence the kind of make up that you do
Kaltego: The most important thing for me is not the event perse, it’s how the person wants to feel, do you want to feel sexy, do you want to feel pretty, do you want to feel natural, do you want to feel dainty, do you want to feel stoic

Katlego – The world has a lot of pressures and I think whether you’re working as a doctor, in corporate or as a cashier you need an outlet, you need something that allows you to feel great to be great, so make up does that for me. If I’m battling at work, didn’t have a great day at work and I wasn’t performing as well. Get home do a beat, the person is happy that really balances me out.



Mac question 1 – Jon how would we define side hustling – what is it all about
Jon – That’s a good question – side hustling by definition you gotta have a job, otherwise it wouldn’t be a side hustle – so it’s doing any other work either than your main job, outside of the main job working hours. There’s a sort of nuance definition where a side job is in your same industry – where a side hustle is somewhere else.
KAYA FM LINK




But you can’t pay for initiative, you can’t pay for passion, you can’t say to someone I give you money and you be passionate. It doesn’t come it’s a voluntary act, side hustle allows you to explore those things and when you’re doing a side hustle the magic is you start to bring those into your main job.
Coffee Shop Link


Scelo: The future of work is evolving and it is evolving because of the advances in technology. For instance it is becoming increasingly easier to work remotely
Mac: Scelo how would you say corporate SA has responded to this side hustling generation, is it receptive of it or is there a push back
Scelo: I mean I wouldn’t call it a push back, it’s just a function of the industry or the market being relatively new in the SOuth African context, so what we see is that corporate sometimes needs a lot of education around that is safe and how to actually integrate a freelancer into their existing team.



People Working in offices, corporate CBD visuals



Bryan Visuals




Mac and Scelo walking/establishing shot




Bryan Washing hands











More Corporate esque viz





Mac and Jon walking at HBS
According to Foster-Pedley businesses and companies embrace the future of work with a slight hesitation



Jon Turns out that 77 percent of South African companies that we surveyed, require people to declare their side hustling,, it turns out that 73 percent of people who are side hustling do tell their companies, so there’s a small percentage there who don’t. And it turns out also that there’s a botu a 5050 split between people who are more or less or extremely positive about side hustling and are slightly negative to extremely negative about side hustling and we need to shift that. This is a brilliant to create employment and new businesses in South Africa.




As the side-hustling trend grows, hobbies become small businesses and employees becomes entrepreneurs -corporations and companies are now playing catch up to this developing trend.
